In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data show a strong correlation between the production of high p T hadrons and the multiplicity of low p T hadrons, but no evidence of a direct correlation between multiplicity and the production of high-p T hadrons.

the data are consistent with the hypothesis that the multiplicity distributions are universal, and that the average charged multiplicity density increases with the number of nucleons participating in the collision.

the multiplicity distributions of charged hadrons in the transverse momentum range from 0.3 to 3.2 GeV/ c, at the ISR energies from 22 to 63 GeV, and for the three angles θ = 10°, 20°, 30°, are consistent with a negative binomial distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data are consistent with the hypothesis that the charged multiplicity density is independent of p T and production angle.
the data are in agreement with the predictions of the Lund model, and that there is no evidence of a transition from a soft to a hard regime in the production of charged hadrons.
the multiplicity distributions are consistent with a negative binomial distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multiplicity distributions are not Poisson, even at the largest values of pseudorapidy.
the charged multiplicity density is not a function of pseudoprapidity and azimuth.
the M (η, φ) distribution is not a function of pseudoparticle transverse momentum.
